issues.strongest_rebuttal: The concurrent-region reading of PumpControl may make a sequential WaterState->MethaneState edge semantically inapplicable if all three states are meant to be simultaneously active; but the exact transition inventory still lacks the edge required by the NL's literal sequential wording, so the absence stands as an exact fact.

issues.basis: fcstm_model.text (three '[*] -> X;' lines with concurrent separators inside PumpControl); canonical_source_ir.model.hierarchy_level=concurrent, concurrent_regions.count=3; inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions (transition:line:6/7/8 all scope=PumpControl source=[*]); NL-CONTRACT-NL3-INIT-1 quote and owner/target binding hints (owner=PumpControl, target=PumpState).
issues.expected: PumpControl must have exactly one owner-local initial pseudostate edge that enters PumpState as the sole first substate, consistent with the NL's sequential narrative in which PumpState is entered first, then WaterState, then MethaneState.
issues.observed: The exact source inventory and closed FCSTM model show PumpControl decomposed into three concurrent regions, each independently owning its own initial pseudostate edge: [*]->PumpState (tr_0002/line:6), [*]->WaterState (tr_0003/line:7), and [*]->MethaneState (tr_0004/line:8). All three edges fire concurrently on entry to PumpControl, so PumpState is not uniquely or exclusively entered first; WaterState and MethaneState are entered simultaneously with it rather than after it.
issues.reason: S2 can only confirm the raw endpoint pair [*]->PumpState exists, which it does; but the contract's semantic obligation is that PumpState is entered first/uniquely under PumpControl, a stronger sequential-ordering property that the frozen S2 predicate cannot express given the concurrent three-way fan-out is out of scope for a simple edge-existence check. This is preserved as a predicate-null W1 candidate rather than silently omitted, since the structural conflict (concurrent regions vs. sequential first-entry) is an exact, precisely bound issue.
issues.requirement_quote: The system first transitions to the PumpState substate, where the pump is activated or controlled.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The exact [*]->PumpState edge required by the contract's owner/target hint does exist in the correct owner scope (PumpControl), which could be read as satisfying a minimal existence-only initial_entry check; however the contract's normative statement requires PumpState to be entered as the first substate in a sequential narrative, and the concurrent fan-out structurally contradicts that unique-first-entry semantics, so the edge's mere presence does not discharge the full obligation.

The closed FCSTM shows PumpControl is a composite with three concurrent regions (region 0: PumpState, region 1: WaterState, region 2: MethaneState), each entered directly by its own [*] initial edge inside PumpControl. There is no sequential transition PumpState->WaterState or WaterState->MethaneState in the closed model's complete transition inventory (only tr_0001..tr_0004, all initial-pseudostate edges); this negative fact is the primary behavioral defect found here (wrong_target on the endpoint contracts already covered structurally, but this lens confirms via the complete inventory and deadlock-frontier diagnostics that these leaf states are terminal dead ends with no outgoing edges at all, which is a genuine deadlock-adjacent consequence). All three leaf states (PumpState, WaterState, MethaneState) are LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING per inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostics and verify_facts non_proved deadlock checks (status=refuted, outgoing_count=0), confirming reachable-nonterminal-no-continuation semantics for each. The NL narrative frames these as a "sequential substate narrative" (NL3/NL4/NL5) where the system moves PumpState->WaterState->MethaneState, but the closed model instead makes these three concurrently-active orthogonal regions with no exit path — this is a structural/behavioral mismatch beyond simple wrong_target: it establishes that none of the three states can ever progress once entered, which is a distinct deadlock/frontier consequence layered on top of the wrong_target endpoint issues. I bind V1(initial_scope) candidates against the two transition_endpoints contracts (NL4-ENDPOINT-1, NL5-ENDPOINT-1) is not appropriate since those are already covered by their own wrong_target property; instead I add a derived deadlock_freedom obligation only if NL establishes an explicit progress obligation. Here NL does not explicitly state that PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState must have further continuation beyond reaching the next substate — the sequential-narrative language IS the continuation obligation NL4/NL5 already state via transition_endpoints, so I do not double an additional deadlock_freedom contract without an explicit response/progress clause. I therefore keep this lens's candidates focused on the two exact missing-edge endpoint facts (S2) plus reinforce with deadlock-frontier facts as supporting basis, and add root reachability / owner entry checks which are satisfied (root->PumpControl exists; PumpControl-local initial edges reach all three named substates) hence omitted. No forbidden-scope entry, no event-consumer obligations, and no termination-state contract is present in the supplied set, so no termination candidate is emitted.
